releases.title: Picks: group deep-links + visible external links
notes: Focus view: each card now shows a tappable chip (e.g. Semiconductors · Leaders) that jumps straight to the Lookup tab for that group — full rotation picture in one tap.
All view: group header names are now tappable too, linking to the same Lookup deep-dive.
Expanded card: Finviz and TradingView links are now pill buttons (more visible), and a new 'Peers in group ↗' button opens the Stage-2 Finviz screener pre-filtered to that industry.
Fixed a bug where the Lookup deep-link showed 'not separately tracked' instead of the group's data.

releases.title: Picks: HoD price-basis toggle
notes: Each expanded stock card now has a [ Last | HoD ] toggle inside the risk panel. Last shows risk from the closing price; HoD shows risk from the prior session's High — the realistic breakout entry price.
Extension (ATR ×50MA), stop distances, and $/share risk all update when you switch to HoD. Bar properties (range/ATR, volatility %) stay on close — they describe the instrument, not your entry.
In HoD mode, 'trim' becomes 'extended' when a stock is over-stretched from entry — same red indicator, different meaning: stretch description, not a position instruction.
Basis resets to Last every time you collapse a card — keeping the default view clean.

releases.title: Focus: tighter criteria + tab descriptions
notes: Focus list now requires stocks to be within 4× ATR of the 50MA (down from 5×) — a tighter actionable zone that cuts the field to your sharpest setups.
Extension penalty now starts at 2.5× ATR instead of 3.5×, so scores reflect a stock's stretch more precisely.
Both All and Focus tabs now show a plain-language description of what's in the list and how it's ranked — no jargon required.

releases.title: Picks: group context, external links, Focus scores in All
notes: Focus cards now show a tappable 'Group · Category' subtitle (e.g. Semiconductors · Leaders) — tap it to jump straight to Lookup for that industry's full rotation picture.
Expanded risk panels in both Focus and All views now include Finviz ↗ and TradingView ↗ links for the stock.
Stocks that qualify for Focus (not over-extended, above 50MA) show their Focus score badge in the All view too — same indigo score as in the Focus list.

releases.title: Lookup: Stage-2 names + Finviz deep-link button
notes: The Lookup tab now shows today's Stage-2 picks from the daily list whenever you look up an industry group that is currently in the leading-group universe — rows sorted least-extended first, expandable risk panel included.

A 'Stage-2 screener ↗' button on every industry and sector lookup opens the tight Stage-2 Finviz screener (20MA>50MA, price>50MA, mid-cap+) pre-filtered for that exact group in a new tab — works for all 144 industries and all 11 sectors.
If the group is not in today's leading groups, the button still appears so you can screen it manually.

releases.title: Picks: Focus list + expandable risk panel
notes: New Focus toggle on the Picks tab surfaces the best actionable setups from the daily pick list — ranked by a blended quality score: group sustained-strength (40%), tightness of the nearest MA stop (40%), and how quiet today's bar was (20%), then discounted for extension beyond 3.5×.
Extension penalty ramps from 0 at 3.5× to a 50% haircut at 5× (the hard-DQ line) — so a stretched name is downranked but not hidden from Focus unless it's truly over-extended.

Tap any row to expand the risk panel: prev-day high (next-session buy trigger), 20MA and 50MA stop levels in price and % and $/share, plus three tightness lines (Range/ATR, Volatility ATR%, Stop distance in ATRs). Score component breakdown is shown in the panel during the tuning period.
Focus resets to All on every tab entry — no stale-Focus confusion when data reloads.

releases.title: Picks tab: daily Stage-2 stocks inside leading groups
notes: New Picks tab shows the daily list of Stage-2 stock picks scraped from leading industry groups — grouped by category (Leaders, Emerging, Accel, RS New High), then by industry, sorted least-extended first.
ATR extension color bands: emerald (≤5×, actionable), amber (5–8×, caution), red (≥8×, trim candidate). Base filter hides micro-caps and stocks not in a Stage-2 configuration.
Five new backend metrics now stored per pick: ATR extension (×50MA), risk to 20MA (%), risk to 50MA (%), day range / ATR tightness, and Stage-2 flag.

releases.title: PWA: sector breadth table in Strength tab
notes: Sector Breadth table now appears in the PWA Strength tab (Industries view): shows how many industries from each sector rank in the top half of the full 144-industry universe by week rank.
Previously this table was only available in the Streamlit dashboard; it is now in the mobile PWA as well.

releases.title: Dashboard: sector filter + breadth table
notes: Streamlit dashboard now has a Sector filter in the sidebar (Industries view). Select any of the 11 sectors to narrow every tab — Snapshot, Top Movers, Time Series, Momentum, Heatmap, Strength — to that sector's industries only.

New Sector Breadth table at the top of the Strength tab (Industries view): shows how many industries from each sector rank in the top half of the full 144-industry universe. Choose week, month, or YTD rank as the lens.

releases.title: Quieter scores: single-day noise removed
notes: Momentum Score now averages 6 timeframes (week → YTD) instead of 7 — the single-day move is excluded because one noisy session could knock a true leader down ~14% for no real reason. Scores are now ~40% steadier day-to-day.
RS Score and the 'beats N/6 tf' count drop the single-day spread the same way. A red day vs the S&P no longer dents a group that's beating the market across every durable horizon.
The day's RS spread is still shown for context — on the vs Market card it now sits behind the 1-month figure rather than leading it.
No action needed: scores recompute automatically.

releases.title: Tap any card to drill into Lookup
notes: Every group card across Momentum, Strength, vs Market, and Today tabs now taps through to the Lookup tab with that group pre-filled.
Subtle › affordance on each card signals tappability. No back-navigation from Lookup — by design for now.

releases.title: Lookup: evict chips, live fuzzy typeahead, always-on momentum chips
notes: Tap × on any recent or pinned chip to remove it without opening the result.
Typing a colloquial name (semis, pharma, banks…) or a near-typo now shows the match in the typeahead dropdown with an ≈ alias or ~ fuzzy badge — no need to submit first.
Top momentum chips now appear below recent and pinned searches, not just when the shelf is empty.

releases.title: AI tab: "Behind this" data provenance drawer
notes: Each AI card now has a collapsible "ⓘ Behind this" section showing the exact computed signals (breadth %, rank movers, RS spreads, divergences) that were fed to the model — so you can see the data behind every conclusion.
Provenance is available for dates on or after today; older dates show no drawer (backward-compatible).
The drawer is read-only and contains only input signals — no raw model response.

releases.title: Movers tab: RS signals, drill-down & rank toggle
notes: Top Gainers now show an NH badge (amber) when a group's RS vs S&P is at a 20-session high, or a ↑ cross badge (sky) when it just flipped from lagging to beating the market — so a rank climber that's also outperforming the market is immediately visible.
The momentum label on each card renamed from 'Score' to 'Mom' for clarity, consistent with the Today tab.
Tap any mover card to jump directly to that group's full Lookup detail (perf history, RS spreads, AI context) — adds it to your recents automatically.
New YTD / Month / Week toggle below the lookback buttons: switch between tracking YTD rank changes (position traders), Month rank (swing), or Week rank (active) without leaving the tab.

releases.title: Momentum tab: confirmed scores + clearer rotation
notes: Momentum cards now headline Confirmed momentum (strength gated by cross-timeframe agreement) instead of the raw score, so broad-based leaders rank above groups riding a single hot timeframe. The raw score is still shown under each name.

Rotation cards now show the actual short- and long-horizon percentile ranks the regime signal is built from (e.g. 'Short 78th · Long 22nd pctile') — these reconcile exactly with the regime number, unlike the old raw-% line.
The Established (balanced) list is now sorted by momentum strength with a divider after the top 3, so the groups closest to rotating in surface first.
Acceleration badges now distinguish 'steady' (~) from 'not enough history yet' (—) instead of showing nothing for both.

releases.title: AI tab: structured desk briefing
notes: The AI tab now leads with a one-line Headline and a Conviction badge (High / Medium / Low) judging how broad and consistent today's read is.
New Rotation Map card spells out capital flow as 'OUT of X → IN to Y' pairs — the core rotation thesis, stated literally.
New Watchlist card surfaces 3–5 specific groups to watch with the exact trigger (RS cross, RS new high, or rank/momentum divergence).
New Relative Strength card calls out which groups are actually beating the S&P 500 (not just leading their peers).
New Risks & Fragility card flags strong-but-slipping and all-green-but-unstable setups so the bullish read stays honest.

Each section is generated by its own focused AI call with purpose-built input data (e.g. the Rotation Map is fed week/month perf, rs_slope and RS-cross flags so it reports real flows instead of guessing pairings; the Watchlist is fed pre-tagged trigger types). Older dates without a briefing still render fine.

releases.title: Strength cards show 'beats N/7' vs S&P
notes: Sustained and All Green cards now carry a 'beats N/7' chip showing how many of the 7 timeframes the group is outperforming the S&P 500.
The chip is colored by RS Score (green = broadly beating the market, red = broadly lagging), so you can tell a true market-beater from a group that's only riding a broad rally.
The chip is hidden when there's no S&P benchmark row for the date — a group is never mislabeled as confirmed when RS data is missing.
Uses existing rs_score / beats_benchmark columns — no pipeline changes.

releases.title: RS discrete flags: NH, ↑ cross, beats SPY
notes: vs Market cards now show an 'NH' (amber) badge when a group's 1-month RS spread vs SPY is at its 20-session high — the classic IBD RS-new-high leadership signal.
'↑ cross' (sky) badge appears when a group just flipped from lagging to beating the market within the last 5 sessions — the earliest-stage rotation trigger.
Sub-line now shows 'beats N/7 tf': how many of the 7 standard timeframes the group is currently outperforming the S&P 500 on.
Both badges appear in the RS Score leaderboard and the Emerging/Fading regime view.
Pipeline: beats_benchmark_{day..ytd}, rs_new_high, rs_cross columns added to deltas.csv — auto-migrates on next compute_deltas.py run.

releases.title: vs Market tab — RS vs S&P 500
notes: New 'vs Mkt' tab shows each sector and industry's relative strength versus the S&P 500, not just versus its peers.
RS Score view ranks groups by how broadly they beat the market across all 7 timeframes (like Momentum Score, but vs SPY instead of vs each other).
Emerging / Fading view surfaces groups whose market-relative edge is freshly building (short-horizon RS outpacing long-horizon) versus those where the RS advantage is stalling.
Today cards now show a '+X.Xpp vs S&P' chip for any non-null RS spread (green/emerald when meaningful, grey when neutral).
RS signals populate automatically once the daily scraper runs — they appear as NaN until the first SPY benchmark snapshot is collected.

releases.title: Start Here intro
notes: New users see a 5-slide welcome tour on first launch — why groups matter, what's different from Finviz, and a one-line tour of all 6 tabs.
Tap the ⓘ icon → Start Here anytime to re-read the intro, or press 'Replay intro' to run the full carousel again.
Cites the O'Neil/IBD stat inline: about half of any stock's move comes from its industry group and sector (37% group + 12% sector).

releases.title: Lookup: recents, pins, fuzzy search, and smart chips
notes: The Lookup tab now remembers your last 8 searches — they appear as chips below the search bar when the input is empty.
Pin any ticker or group from its result card (☆ Pin) to keep it permanently at the top of the chip shelf, surviving the 8-item recents cap.
Type a colloquial name like 'semis', 'pharma', 'banks', or 'biotech' — built-in synonyms resolve it to the exact Finviz group instantly.
Made a typo? Fuzzy matching catches near-misses (e.g. 'semiconductrs') and shows a one-tap 'Did you mean Semiconductors?' prompt.
When the Lookup tab is fresh (no history, no typing), it shows your top momentum groups for the day as suggestion chips.

releases.title: ETF lookups fixed + Lookup group search
notes: ETF lookups now show their true sector or industry. COPX shows Basic Materials › Copper, ITA shows Industrials › Aerospace & Defense, SMH shows Technology › Semiconductors — not "Financial / Asset Management" (which was what FMP reports for all fund entities).
Thematic ETFs (COPX, ITA, SMH, SOXX, XBI, IBB, GDX, GDXJ, URA, TAN, JETS, XOP, OIH, KRE, KBE) now show their holdings theme with a blue badge.
Sector SPDR ETFs (XLE, XLF, XLI, XLK, XLV, XLP, XLY, XLU, XLB, XLRE, XLC) show the sector card and a "Sector ETF" badge — no industry card since they span all industries.
Broad market ETFs (SPY, QQQ, VTI, DIA, IWM) show an informational card explaining they track the full market — no single rotation group applies.
Type a sector or industry name in the Lookup tab — it resolves instantly from cached data, zero network calls (e.g. Semiconductors, Energy, Technology).
Typeahead dropdown appears as you type (≥ 2 chars): up to 6 matches, matched text highlighted, keyboard-navigable (↑ ↓ Enter Esc).
Group cards now show a full deep-dive: all 7 timeframe ranks and performance %s, YTD rank deltas, and a momentum section (confirmed, acceleration, regime, rank trend).

releases.title: Guide & What's New hub
notes: New ℹ️ button opens a built-in Guide explaining every metric, color, arrow, and threshold — no external docs needed.
Unseen-update dot on ℹ️ and a one-time banner let you know when something new has shipped.
The Guide legend reads the app's live threshold constants, so it can never drift out of sync.
Rotation signal fixed: short horizon is now week + month (day was too noisy); long horizon is 3mo + 6mo + year.
Phase-history strip on AI cards redesigned as a clean CSS timeline — graduated opacity, a connecting line, and dates on both ends.
The 'vs 20d ago' row on an expanded Today card is now explained in the Guide — tap it to learn how performance change differs from rank change.
The Guide now covers the AI tab too: Rotation Phase and the AI daily note are explained, with a tap-through ⓘ on the Rotation Phase card.

releases.title: Momentum signals on every card
notes: Momentum cards show an acceleration badge (▲▲ / ▲ / ▼ / ▼▼) so you can see momentum building or fading at a glance.
New Rotation sub-view in the Momentum tab splits groups into Emerging / Established / Fading based on the regime signal.
Today cards gain a rank-trend arrow (↑↑ / ↑ / ~ / ↓ / ↓↓) and a performance-delta context row when you expand a card.
Strength tab is now sorted by confirmed momentum (strength × cross-timeframe consistency).
Lookback buttons are derived straight from your data — no hard-coded values.
Momentum/Rotation sub-view preference is remembered between visits.

releases.title: Trading-day lookbacks & richer signals
notes: Lookback windows switched from calendar days to trading sessions: 5 / 10 / 20 / 50 days — weekends and holidays no longer skew the deltas.
Six new computed signals: confirmed momentum, weighted momentum (mid- and fast-horizon), acceleration, regime (emerging vs. fading), rank-trend slope, and rank agreement.
All momentum columns are now derived from a single config, so the pipeline, dashboard, and PWA always stay in sync.

releases.title: Lookup tab: moaty metrics
notes: Lookup now shows a weekly-rank sparkline so you can see at a glance whether a group's rank has been rising or falling.
Rank Floor shows the worst rank across 1mo / 3mo / 6mo — a Sustained or Consistent conviction chip appears when the floor clears the bar.
Breadth dot strip (D·W·M·Q·6M·Y) shows which timeframes are positive; an All-Green badge fires when the meaningful ones all confirm.
The Signal card now cites concrete evidence — rank trajectory, conviction, momentum percentile — instead of a bare label.
One-tap deep links to Finviz and TradingView charts added to every ticker result.
Weekend and NYSE-holiday phantom dates eliminated: snapshots are always stamped with the real trading day.

releases.title: AI notes rebuilt as plain-English
notes: The AI briefing is now a single readable note per group instead of a rigid structured format that sometimes leaked raw JSON or went blank.
Notes are built directly from computed signals — sustained strength, movers, momentum leaders and laggards, divergences — so they always render cleanly.
Ticker Lookup goes live: Worker deployed to the edge, PWA Lookup tab and Streamlit tab both wired to it.

releases.title: Ticker Lookup
notes: New Lookup tab: type any ticker to instantly see its Finviz sector and industry, company profile, and how those groups are ranking right now.
Results are cached at the edge so repeat lookups return in milliseconds.
AI tab date navigation: Prev / Next arrows let you browse past briefings without the buttons ever getting stuck.

releases.title: AI notes: smarter generation & reliability
notes: Fixed a daily-quota bug that could leave today's AI note half-written or missing — partial results now resume and fill in only what's needed.
AI generation now runs in its own workflow step so collection and analysis are independent; a failed scrape no longer blocks the briefing.
Smart-skip logic: if the data hasn't changed since the last run, the AI step skips redundant API calls.

releases.title: A richer AI tab
notes: Key-signal bullets, a collapsible briefing, and conviction tags make the AI note faster to scan.
Rotation phase and a top-sector watchlist with thesis now appear alongside the briefing.
A 'what changed' delta card shows how today's read compares to yesterday's.
Relative timestamp, native share sheet, and a phase-history strip added.
Browse back through any past date using the date-navigation arrows.
New sort options added to Today tab: Qtr %, 6-Month %, and 1-Year % (7 sort options total); rank badge circles now show 6-month rank.

releases.title: AI Insights tab launches
notes: New AI tab surfaces a nightly plain-English briefing for both sectors and industries, generated by Gemini.
Includes a rotation-phase read (Early / Mid / Late Cycle / Defensive) and a top-sector watchlist with investment thesis.
Workflow monitoring added: each pipeline run now logs AI outcome (complete / partial / skipped) so you can see at a glance whether today's note is fresh.

releases.title: Strength tab, AI pipeline & PWA polish
notes: New Strength tab: Sustained Strength surfaces groups that are top-ranked across month, quarter, and half simultaneously. All-Green flags every timeframe positive.
New rank-agreement signal (0–1) measures how consistently a group ranks across timeframes — 1.0 means all confirm the same standing.
Pull-to-refresh, persistent preferences (group/sort/lookback survive app close), and search filtering added to the PWA.
iOS Add-to-Home-Screen icon added; errors now show on the active tab instead of silently failing.
Data freshness timestamp now shows in Pacific time in the PWA header.
Haptic feedback fires when pull-to-refresh crosses the release threshold.

releases.title: Finviz Groups Tracker launches
notes: Daily scraper captures all Finviz sector and industry groups every trading day via Playwright — no API subscription required.
Ranks and rank/performance deltas computed daily; rank 1 is always the strongest performer across that timeframe.
Installable iPhone PWA (Safari → Add to Home Screen) with Today, Movers, and Momentum tabs from day one.
Today tab shows color-coded performance cards; Movers ranks groups by how much their YTD rank has shifted; Momentum shows the running momentum score.
Companion Streamlit dashboard adds snapshot tables, multi-group time series, a performance heatmap, and CSV download.
GitHub Actions runs the full pipeline daily and emails on failure — no manual intervention needed.
